data.text: The evidence is consistent and complete. Summary of what I observed:

data.reason: The ISP link dropped when the cable modem lost upstream ranging ("No Ranging Response received - T3 time-out" at 02:01:44) and then re-registered without a valid provisioned config ("TFTP failed - configuration file NOT FOUND"), so the WAN path through the provider is broken even though the modem now reports OPERATIONAL; the firewall's own WAN state (lease + default route via 198.51.100.1) is stale from before that event and no reload was ever applied because the watchdog runs in observe mode.

data.cause: The ISP link dropped when the cable modem lost upstream ranging ("No Ranging Response received - T3 time-out" at 02:01:44) and then re-registered without a valid provisioned config ("TFTP failed - configuration file NOT FOUND"), so the WAN path through the provider is broken even though the modem now reports OPERATIONAL; the firewall's own WAN state (lease + default route via 198.51.100.1) is stale from before that event and no reload was ever applied because the watchdog runs in observe mode.
evidence: cat /var/db/wan-watchdog/modem-events.jsonl — 2026-03-03 02:01:44 id 82000200 'No Ranging Response received - T3 time-out' (matches the ~02:01 outage start), 02:14:10 id 68000407 'TFTP failed - configuration file NOT FOUND', 02:28:21 id 90000000 'Cable Modem Reboot because of - unknown; registration complete'

cat /var/db/wan-watchdog/modem-metrics.jsonl — 02:06 status NOT_SYNCHRONIZED, then OPERATIONAL at 02:29 and 02:40 but with uncorrected codewords climbing 112 -> 131 and corrected 40211 -> 52070 (worst uncorrected 615), i.e. a damaged provider downstream while nominally registered
ping -c 3 -n 198.51.100.1 on gw.lan — 3 packets transmitted, 0 received, 100% loss to the ISP modem that is the default gateway, so nothing beyond the provider hand-off is reachable

arp -a -n — 198.51.100.1 still resolves to 00:17:10:9a:a3:96 with a live expiry, and ifconfig vtnet0 shows UP,RUNNING,LOWER_UP, active, so the local WAN NIC/cabling is fine and the failure is above the LAN-side of the modem

netstat -rn — default route still via 198.51.100.1 dev vtnet0; cat /var/db/dhclient.leases.vtnet0 keeps fixed-address 198.51.100.27 with renew 2026/3/5, so dhclient will not refresh this pre-reboot state on its own

cat /var/db/wan-watchdog/state.json + events.jsonl — outage_start 02:06, decision 'none' (modem_not_operational) at 02:06, 'none' (modem_settling) at 02:29, then action 'reload' / 'would_reload' at 02:30 and again at 02:40 with reloads_in_outage=2, i.e. the watchdog judged a WAN reload due but never applied it because mode is observe
data.recommendation: Report the outage to the ISP/cable operator: give them the modem log timestamps (T3 ranging timeout 02:01:44, TFTP config file NOT FOUND 02:14:10, reboot + registration complete 02:28:21) and the rising uncorrected/FEC codeword counts, and ask them to fix the plant signal and re-provision the modem's config file. In parallel, apply the pending WAN reload on gw.lan to drop the stale pre-reboot lease/route so the firewall renegotiates once the provider side is healthy, and consider taking the wan-watchdog out of observe mode so its already-computed reload actually fires instead of only being logged. Local services are unaffected, so no local DNS/DHCP/firewall changes are needed.
data.detail: ISP-side cable plant / provisioning fault on the modem uplink (T3 ranging timeout, then missing config file); gateway WAN state now stale
